q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT b.name AS beer, s.bar, s.price FROM beer AS b LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.beer WHERE s.price IS NULL OR s.price = (SELECT MIN(price) FROM serves WHERE beer = b.name)

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses a subquery to find the minimum price for each beer and then joins it with the 'serves' table, while Q2 directly joins the 'beer' and 'serves' tables and filters the results based on the minimum price. This can lead to different results if there are multiple bars serving the same beer at the same price, as Q1 will return all such bars, while Q2 will return only one of them.
